title: Patrol Pro
subtitle: An Arduino safety module for an autonomous patrol robot.
summary: Tuned flame and gas sensing on an Arduino Mega and integrated visible and audible warnings for an indoor patrol robot.
overview: Patrol Pro is an HKU group project that combines an Arduino Mega control layer with Jetson Nano perception. My work focused on the Arduino hazard response. I compared baseline and exposure readings, set sensor-specific thresholds, and connected fire and gas alert states to onboard warnings.
contributions: Implemented and tested the Arduino smoke and fire detection module. Measured baseline and flame-triggered readings across the front, side, and rear sensor positions.
Tested the MQ-2 response under gas and smoke exposure and tuned the detection threshold to limit false alerts during the demonstration.
Integrated the fire and gas alert states with the LED, OLED, and buzzer outputs.
Helped run the final demo, planned and edited most of the product video, and documented sensor behavior and threshold logic for the team report.

features.title: Flame sensing around the chassis
features.body: A front five-channel IR detector and side and rear IR sensors sample for flame from different positions around the robot.

features.title: Gas and smoke sensing
features.body: The Arduino polls the MQ-2 alongside the IR sensors and evaluates its readings against a separately tuned threshold.

features.title: Local hazard warnings
features.body: The fire or gas state drives LED, OLED, and buzzer outputs so the alert is visible and audible on the robot.

features.title: Team patrol and monitoring
features.body: Teammates handled Jetson vision, person detection, face and QR verification, and the dashboard and incident logging. Chassis integration was shared.

challenges.title: Handle opposite flame sensor readings
challenges.problem: The front detector started low and rose when exposed to flame. Side and rear sensors started high and dropped sharply near a direct flame.
challenges.solution: I measured the baseline and hazard readings at each position. I used a rising threshold for the front array and a falling threshold for the side and rear sensors.

challenges.title: Tune for the gradual MQ-2 response
challenges.problem: Gas and smoke exposure produced a smaller, slower change than the IR sensors. Threshold placement affected how easily the robot raised a false alert.
challenges.solution: I compared normal readings with readings during exposure and tuned the MQ-2 threshold separately, then repeated the sensor-triggered demo sequence.

challenges.title: Coordinate several warnings from one state
challenges.problem: A hazard needed to produce a consistent visible and audible warning during the demo.
challenges.solution: I connected the warning outputs to the Arduino fire and gas states so they followed the same hazard decision.

architecture.caption: The IR and MQ-2 sensors feed the Arduino in parallel. Sensor-specific threshold checks determine a fire or gas state, which drives the onboard warnings. The team’s Jetson perception and dashboard are outside this module diagram.

results.label: Flame sensor response
results.detail: The original project portfolio records a rise at the front detector and a drop at the side and rear sensors.

results.label: Onboard warning integration
results.detail: The module connects the hazard state to the LED, OLED, and buzzer.

results.label: Sensor-triggered checks
results.detail: The project portfolio documents repeated checks on the robot and includes photos of the warning response and a link to the team demo.

boundaries: The available evidence is the original project portfolio and team demo. Firmware and raw readings were unavailable for independent review.
The documented checks cover demo conditions. Detection range, response time, false-alert rate, and safety certification are unverified.

title: StudyPilot

summary: Course-material workflows and study planning across a React interface, Spring Boot APIs, and a Python service.
overview: StudyPilot connects course materials, assessment schedules, availability, and study tasks. My contribution is in the integration: plan and task APIs, data transfer between services, material flows, and Study Room features. The current code also includes a deterministic planning core, whose complete original authorship I do not claim.
contributions: Contributed assessment, study-plan, and task API changes, including Java DTOs, service logic, and frontend wiring.
Connected course-material input and Study Room lecture flows across React, Spring Boot, and Python.

challenges.solution: I contributed typed transfer objects, service calls, and API wiring so these concepts can move through the stack without being hidden in interface-only state.
